## Summary of findings (and an important limitation)

I must be upfront: **the tools available to me cannot retrieve the full blood-concentration dataset in bulk.** Here is what I established after probing every relevant tool:

- The fields `Blood concentration - Conc. blood IM [pg/L]`, `Blood concentration - Conc. blood MS [pg/L]`, and `Secretome location` exist, but they are returned **only** by the single-protein endpoints (`get_protein_info` / `get_protein_by_ensembl`).
- `search_proteins`, `advanced_search`, and `batch_protein_lookup` all ignore the `columns` parameter and return only the summary list fields (Gene/Ensembl/description/Uniprot/Chromosome/Protein class/Evidence). There is no filter for "has both IM and MS," and no bulk export of the concentration columns.
- Therefore I can only inspect proteins one at a time, and I could not enumerate the complete set of proteins that have **both** an immunoassay and a mass-spectrometry value (ALB, for example, has IM = 4×10¹³ but MS = null, so it is excluded).

Because of this, I **cannot** generate the requested scatter plot, the top-15 diverging bar chart, or the headline secretome-location count — those require the full population, which is not obtainable with these tools. **Any such numbers I gave would be fabricated, so I am not providing them.**

## What I *can* verify from actual tool results

The only proteins I retrieved that have **both** concentrations are these three (all `Secretome location` = "Secreted to blood"):

| Gene | Secretome location | IM [pg/L] | MS [pg/L] | log10(IM) | log10(MS) | log10 ratio (IM/MS) |
|------|--------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------------------|
| APOA1 | Secreted to blood | 1,450,000,000,000 (1.45×10¹²) | 160,000,000,000 (1.6×10¹¹) | 12.161 | 11.204 | 0.957 |
| SERPINA1 | Secreted to blood | 1,920,000,000,000 (1.92×10¹²) | 230,000,000,000 (2.3×10¹¹) | 12.283 | 11.362 | 0.922 |
| TTR | Secreted to blood | 345,000,000,000 (3.45×10¹¹) | 69,000,000,000 (6.9×10¹⁰) | 11.538 | 10.839 | 0.699 |

Notes on the arithmetic:
- log10(IM) = exponent + log10(mantissa), e.g. APOA1 = 12 + log10(1.45) = 12.161.
- log10 ratio = log10(IM) − log10(MS); e.g. APOA1 = 12.161 − 11.204 = 0.957 (equivalently log10(9.06) = 0.957).
- All three log10 ratios are **positive**, i.e. immunoassay exceeds mass spectrometry — consistent with the known pattern that immunoassays often read higher than MS for abundant plasma proteins.

(ALB, which I also checked, has IM = 4×10¹³ but **MS = null**, so it does not qualify and would be excluded from this analysis.)

I would need either:
1. a tool that returns the concentration + secretome columns in bulk (or honors the `columns` parameter / allows filtering on "has both IM and MS"), or
2. permission to query the full protein list individually so I can assemble the population, rank the discordance, and build the scatter/bar charts.

As it stands, with the data I could actually retrieve, the complete-set scatter plot, the 15 most-discordant diverging bars, and the secretome-location count **cannot be produced from tool results**, and I will not estimate them.

| Gene | Secretome location | IM [pg/L] | MS [pg/L] | log10(IM) | log10(MS) | log10 ratio (IM/MS) |
|------|--------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------------------|
| APOA1 | Secreted to blood | 1,450,000,000,000 (1.45×10¹²) | 160,000,000,000 (1.6×10¹¹) | 12.161 | 11.204 | 0.957 |
| SERPINA1 | Secreted to blood | 1,920,000,000,000 (1.92×10¹²) | 230,000,000,000 (2.3×10¹¹) | 12.283 | 11.362 | 0.922 |
| TTR | Secreted to blood | 345,000,000,000 (3.45×10¹¹) | 69,000,000,000 (6.9×10¹⁰) | 11.538 | 10.839 | 0.699 |

Notes on the arithmetic:
- log10(IM) = exponent + log10(mantissa), e.g. APOA1 = 12 + log10(1.45) = 12.161.
- log10 ratio = log10(IM) − log10(MS); e.g. APOA1 = 12.161 − 11.204 = 0.957 (equivalently log10(9.06) = 0.957).
- All three log10 ratios are **positive**, i.e. immunoassay exceeds mass spectrometry — consistent with the known pattern that immunoassays often read higher than MS for abundant plasma proteins.

(ALB, which I also checked, has IM = 4×10¹³ but **MS = null**, so it does not qualify and would be excluded from this analysis.)
